scope: Tokitai v0.10.x: code-review deferred findings batch (post M-0.9.1 hotfix ship at HEAD 31d34ea)
philosophy_anchor: Preserve the in-process compile-time dispatch advantage. Every new task must justify itself by exploiting the compile-time seam that runtime-only competitors cannot reach. Hard constraint: no dependency on `rmcp` or any other MCP SDK; spec is pinned via fixture + manual re-sync, not a moving dep.

differentiating_strategy.thesis: Tokitai is the only Rust tool-calling stack where schema, dispatch, security policy, and observability are produced by a proc-macro over a typed surface. M-0.9.0 added three compile-time defenses (adversarial description lint, capability manifest, cross-crate version assertion). M-0.9.1 remediated 8 code-review findings discovered by a 4-lens adversarial-verification review. v4.0 addresses the remaining deferred items (18 low/medium findings) as a consolidation pass.

pillars_we_reject: Becoming a second MCP SDK. We do not chase spec-conformance market share; rmcp does that. Hard rule reaffirmed: no rmcp or any other MCP SDK as a dependency.
Runtime plugin / hot-reload as a first-class model. It conflicts with the compile-time schema pillar; we add a non-default `DynamicToolProvider` trait instead (T-010, shipped).
LLM-provider SDK features (streaming, prompt caching, context-window math). Tokitai's job ends at `call_tool`.
Replacing the macro pipeline (syn/quote -> something else). All changes are additive or surgical.
Adding features with no test surface. Every task in v4.0 ships with a fixture / test / trybuild entry.
Re-introducing features that were already shipped under a different name.

non_goals: Become a second rmcp - hardcoded NO. T-005 implements stdio MCP directly; T-021 adds the typed handle layer; both rules extend to all v4.0 tasks.
Rewrite the macro pipeline (syn/quote -> something else). All changes are additive or surgical.
Add features that have no test surface.
Match the LLM-side harness surface (LangChain's AgentExecutor, AutoGen's groups, CrewAI's crews). Tokitai is below that layer.
Take a runtime-detection stance on prompt injection. v4.0's consolidation is compile-time + manifest.

new_tasks.title: Adversarial description lint follow-ups: non-ASCII coverage, CSV robustness, perf string allocation, trybuild anchor
new_tasks.north_star: T-022's coverage gaps (non-ASCII positive-list test, CSV-no-escape for comma in values, trybuild docs.rs anchor existence, per-desc String allocation in doc claim) are closed.
new_tasks.rationale: The 4-lens code review found several T-022 follow-ups that are individually small but collectively worth tracking as a single task. None is a security regression (T-022 already fires on all non-ASCII via the byte-check added in M-0.9.1 C-3), but the absence of test coverage and doc/perf consistency weakens the maintainability of the defense.
acceptance_criteria: Add a positive-list test in `desc_safety_test.rs` that exercises `contains_only_ascii_printable` with tab (0x09), newline (0x0A), carriage return (0x0D), and a mixed ASCII-only string (0x20-0x7E) — all must pass cleanly. Already covers non-ASCII rejection via C-3 test fixture.

Add whitespace-around-comma coverage for `split_blocklist` in `tokitai-macros/src/description/safety.rs`: `"a, b, c"` should parse to `["a", "b", "c"]` (trimmed). Current implementation does not trim; add a test + fix the parsing.

Add a CSV-escape mechanism for `desc_blocklist`: a comma-containing literal like `"ignore previous, and then"` must be expressible. Minimum: support double-quote wrapping in the env-var CSV parser, or document the limitation and add a trybuild fixture that demonstrates the workaround (use per-tool `desc_blocklist` for comma values).

Verify that the `docs.rs errors.html#E0032` anchor referenced in `tests/ui/desc_safety_injection.stderr` exists on the published tokitai-macros crate. If it does not exist, either create the anchor or change the reference to a valid docs.rs URL.
Update `docs/AI_INTEGRATION.md` table row for T-022 per-call cost from "Zero" to "O(len(desc)) at macro time (allocates for blocklist merge)" to match the implementation.

new_tasks.title: Capability manifest ergonomics: better diagnostics, empty-Vec alloc fix, W023 first-class opt-out
new_tasks.north_star: The capability manifest system has no silent failure modes: every missing declaration triggers a visible diagnostic, every denied capability names the allowlist, and the generated code allocates no Vec for empty slices.
new_tasks.rationale: The code review found 8 ergonomic gaps in T-023's implementation. Most are diagnostic-quality improvements (span at the offending entry rather than the method ident, Display impl missing the allowlist, W023 message missing cross-reference to other `allow` uses). One is a perf regression (Vec allocation for empty CAPABILITIES slice). One is a correctness gap: the `#[tool(requires_invalid)]` flag is silently dropped before the const is emitted.
acceptance_criteria: `CapabilityNotInAllowlist::Display` (in `tokitai-mcp-server/src/server.rs`) names the configured allowlist in the error message, so an operator triaging the failure doesn't need to cross-reference config.

The `#[tool(requires = [...])]` parse-error diagnostic anchors at the offending entry's span, not at the method's ident span. (Currently at method ident; change to the individual entry span in the `requires` list.)

`W023` warning message (in `tokitai-macros/src/tool/mod.rs`) includes a cross-reference to other `allow = [...]` uses (like `allow_short_desc`, `allow_insecure_desc`) so the user knows the suppression pattern is consistent.

`generate_capabilities_consts` in `definitions.rs` skips Vec allocation when `tools` slice is empty (the `CAPABILITIES` const still resolves as `&[]` via a zero-capacity vec or a static reference, not an allocated empty Vec).
`CAN_INVALID` / `requires_invalid` flagged entries are NOT silently dropped before CAPABILITIES const emission — either emit them with an error or document the limitation.
Add a `parse_blocklist_env` visibility reduction: `pub fn` → `pub(crate) fn` (it is only used inside the macros crate and expanding visibility beyond the crate is an accidental API leak).

new_tasks.title: TypedDispatcher and serve() hardening: tools_list caching, env-args integration test
new_tasks.north_star: TypedDispatcher::tools_list is memoized (cached) so repeated calls don't re-validate every spec. The serve() entry point's argument parsing is exercised with real std::env::args in an integration test.
new_tasks.rationale: Two deferred findings from code review: (1) TypedDispatcher::tools_list re-scans every spec on every call — since the spec set is immutable after construction, the result can be cached in the OnceLock. (2) parse_serve_args is unit-tested with a fake argv but never with real std::env::args from an integration test, leaving the boundary where env::args() returns unexpected values unexercised.
acceptance_criteria: TypedDispatcher::tools_list — when called multiple times with the same spec set — returns the cached result after the first call. Cache is a `OnceLock<Vec<...>>` or similar. Test: call tools_list twice and assert pointer equality (same allocation) OR assert time (second call is ~instant).

Add an integration test in `tokitai-mcp-server/tests/version_assertion_test.rs` that calls `serve()` (or its argument-parsing equivalent) with real `std::env::args()` by exercising the binary entry point. If a pure test is impossible, add a doc example or a smoke-test shell script in `examples/`.
Both changes pass CI with no new top-level deps.

new_tasks.title: Code quality / API surface cleaning pass: duplicate docs, undocumented alias, lazy env-var probe
new_tasks.north_star: The public API surface has no duplicate doc comments, no undocumented function aliases, and the env-var probes in the hot macro path are lazy.
new_tasks.rationale: Six low-severity findings from code review that don't belong to any feature-specific task but are worth fixing for consistency: (1) duplicate doc comments on CapabilityManifestProvider trait and capability_in_allowlist; (2) undocumented `run_version_check` alias for `serve`; (3) `category` parsed and stored in a local variable with no error code for silent fall-through; (4) `TOKITAI_PROFILE` / `TOKITAI_QUIET` probed at every macro invocation (not lazy); (5) assert_compatible_with panic messages still do not name the drifted versions (partially addressed by H-1 doc claim fix but implementation remains); (6) T-022 env-var forwarding has no validation that value is non-pathological.
acceptance_criteria: Duplicate doc comments on `capability_in_allowlist` (tokitai-core/src/lib.rs ~line 2807) are deduplicated: keep the richer one, remove the orphaned line or merge into the parent item.

`run_version_check` alias for `serve` (tokitai-mcp-server/src/lib.rs:~line 129) is either documented with a `///` doc-comment noting its relationship to `serve()`, or removed in favor of a single entry point.
`category` parsing in `tokitai-macros/src/tool/attrs/method.rs` ~line 665: add an error code for the fall-through case (category set but unused) or remove the variable.

`should_show_warnings()` and `profiling_enabled()` calls in tok-macros/src/tool/mod.rs are hoisted out of the per-method loop into the per-impl-block scope (they only need to be probed once per impl block, not once per method).

`assert_compatible_with` panic messages name both the expected and actual version (currently hardcoded drift-category strings). This may require accepting `const_format_args!` is not stable; use `concat!` in a non-const runtime helper called from the const-eval path.

`TOKITAI_DESC_BLOCKLIST` env-var value forwarded by `tokitai-macros/build.rs` is validated as UTF-8 and non-empty (currently forwarded verbatim without validation; a binary payload in the env var crashes the macro).

previously_open_questions_now_resolved.resolution: T-005 ships without rmcp. T-021 adds the typed MCP handle layer without rmcp. T-023's capability manifest lives in tokitai-core and tokitai-macros; no rmcp. Hard rule reaffirmed for all v3.0 tasks.
T-010 shipped with a new DynamicToolProvider trait, non-breaking, opt-in.
T-010's design choice of a new trait preserves compile-time as the default and promotes dynamic to first-class via opt-in.
T-012 shipped with mcp as the default dialect. Re-evaluation deferred via telemetry.
T-013 shipped with any-string accepted; version_policy = semver enables ordered comparison.
T-016 shipped with both example = call!(...) and examples = [call!(...), ...].
T-016 embeds don't evaluate: inlines literal args + literal result, runs type checker.
T-017 ships with sequential-only. Parallel is tracked enhancement.
T-022 uses per-build env var TOKITAI_DESC_BLOCKLIST with in-source conservative default. docs/AI_INTEGRATION.md documents the env var with a security-team-runbook example.
T-023 uses glob in allowlist (trailing-* prefix match), exact in tool's declaration. Documented in MCP_ARCHITECTURE.md.
T-023 uses stringly-typed &str for v1. Typed enum is a v2 add-on.
T-024 uses hard refusal (exit 78) by default with --allow-tokitai-mismatch escape hatch. Logged at warn! level.
